title: 2020 AMC 12A Problem 15
statement: In the complex plane, let \(A\) be the set of solutions to \(z^3 - 8 = 0\) and let \(B\) be the set of solutions to \(z^3 - 8z^2 - 8z + 64 = 0.\) What is the greatest distance between a point of \(A\) and a point of \(B?\)

solutions.text:
The set \(A\) consists of the cube roots of \(8:\) \(2,\) \(-1 + i\sqrt3,\) and \(-1 - i\sqrt3.\)

Factoring by grouping, \(z^3 - 8z^2 - 8z + 64\) \(= z^2(z - 8) - 8(z - 8)\) \(= (z - 8)(z^2 - 8),\) so \(B = \{8, 2\sqrt2, -2\sqrt2\},\) all real.

The greatest distance is from \(-1 \pm i\sqrt3\) to \(8:\) \(\sqrt{(8 - (-1))^2 + (\sqrt3)^2}\) \(= \sqrt{81 + 3}\) \(= \sqrt{84} = 2\sqrt{21}.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: \(A\) is the three cube roots of \(8;\) factor the second cubic by grouping
The largest distance pairs a nonreal cube root of \(8\) with the farthest real root of the second equation
